newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY OIL ACTIVITY BOOM TO CONTINUE - WOODMAC.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY OIL ACTIVITY BOOM TO CONTINUE - WOODMAC.

text.p: Development activity in the oil and gas sector on the Norwegian continental shelf is booming and production of crude and natural gas liquids (NGLs) is continuing to set record levels, oil industry analysts Wood Mackenzie said on Monday.

"In general terms, the next few years will see a high pace of development activity in Norway, with the bulk of the activity being located in the northern North Sea, and mid-Norway emerging as a major province," Wood Mackenzie said in a review.

Norwegian authorities have approved 12 fields and three pipelines for development since the beginning of 1996. Wood Mackenzie said a delay in deciding large-scale gas allocations made it difficult to predict the order of development of gas fields.
"However, we now consider 12 fields to be probable developments which will come onstream over the period 1997-2001, seven of which are new inclusions for 1997."

Wood Mackenzie said these fields have total reserves of 1.2 billion barrels of oil/NGLs and 4.9 trillion cubic feet of gas. Capital investment requirements for development were estimated at 41 billion crowns.
"Capital expenditure offshore Norway is now expected to peak this year at around 54 billion crowns and to remain above 40 billion crowns per annum in 1998 and 1999," it added.

Oil/NGL production was forecast to rise from 3.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in 1997 to 3.7 million bpd in 1998, before peaking at 3.8 million bpd in 1999 and remaining at that level for the next two years.
The report said a key theme to emerge in Norway was the impact of reserve upgrades, especially on existing producing fields.

"We estimate that our 1997 portfolio of producing fields and those currently under development have recorded a net upgrade of around 1.5 billion barrels of oil/NGLs and 1.2 trillion cubic feet of gas compared with our 1996 portfolio, a total of 1.7 billion barrels of oil equivalent (boe)," it said.
It added that the most significant opgrades came from the Ekofisk area fields, Heidrun, Statfjord, Troll East and Snorre.
In corporate terms, commercial recoverable reserves increased substantially for most companies active in Norway in oil equivalent terms.

"If upgrades on our existing and new probable developments are included, the overall commercial reserve base in Norway increased by 2.2 billion barrels of oil/NGLs and 7.1 trillion cubic feet of gas over the last year.

"This translates to 15 percent of the remaining recoverable commercial oil/NGL reserves (14.6 billion barrels) and nine percent of the remaining recoverable commercial gas reserves (72 trillion cubic feet) in Norway.".

The combined share in the upgrades of the state's direct financial interest and of state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) amounted to 1.41 billion boe, or 47 percent of the total.

Wood Mackenzie said that in terms of percentage gains relative to the analysts' assessment of reserve position last year, the following companies made gains in the 10 to 30 percent range: Idemitsu (18 percent), Total (14 percent), Phillips (12 percent), Fina (12 percent), Deminex (11 percent) and Norsk Hydro (11 percent).
